messages:
jane-support: Customer (acme-inc) just escalated — p99 spike on text-generation endpoints during their peak at 11:40 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/acme/latency — large jump from 300ms -> 2.1s for p99, p95 up ~700ms. They say errors were 500s and some timeouts. Marking P2 for now.

mike-sre: looking. Any correlation with scale events or provisioning?

jane-support: initial correlation shows a flurry of scale-up events, a bunch of 'cold_gpu_attach' in the logs + attach retries. No obvious auth failures. I captured a sample request_id: r-q2b7n.

carlos-platform: do we have fairshare adjustments running? I see several capacity requests back-to-back from the eu-west cluster. Could be fairshare scheduler jitter causing delayed placements.

anya-ml: also saw KV cache misses for the same timeframe; model shard warming took extra seconds. Might be model cache init + coldstart compounding scale latency.

mike-sre: repro steps I'm running: 1) fire 200 concurrent sessions to the dedicated pool 2) observe attach queue 3) watch provisioner logs. Patch to tail: ``kubectl -n provisioner logs -f deploy/provisioner | grep attach``.

ops-bot: @mike-sre provisioner-alert: attach_queue_length=42 attach_failures=3 last_attach_time_ms=18200

mike-sre: confirmed. The attach latencies match. I also see backoff jitter in the fairshare allocator where multiple requests got randomized backoff windows aligned, causing a thundering-burst effect when they all retry.

jane-support: customer mentioned a billing window spike — could burst of tokenization/embeddings at billing boundary have triggered this? They ran a large batch job at 11:39.

carlos-platform: yes — batch jobs are lower priority but still upstreamed to dedicated. Fairshare settings currently: min_reserve=0, burst_quota=1000, jitter_enabled=true. Suggest temporarily increasing min_reserve for their pool and disabling jitter for critical pools.

anya-ml: mitigation idea: pre-warm model cache before attaching GPUs. We can queue a lightweight warmup request when pool scale is triggered. Simple patch: on attach success call warmup_endpoint with small prompt.

mike-sre: quick mitigations I can push now: 1) raise min_reserve to 2 for acme's reserved pool 2) disable randomized backoff for that pool 3) bump pool min size (min-pool = 2) 4) enable immediate warmup hook. Will roll to eu-west first.

jane-support: pls notify customer of rollback plan and ETA. They're sensitive to downtime.

mike-sre: rolling now to eu-west. Command used: ``redwoodctl pool update --pool acme-dedicated --set min_reserve=2,min_size=2,backoff.jitter=false,warmup_hook=true``. Will monitor.

ops-bot: change-audit: user=mike-sre cmd=pool update pool=acme-dedicated delta="min_reserve:0->2,min_size:0->2,backoff.jitter:true->false,warmup_hook:false->true" status=ok

mike-sre: after changes p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 380ms within 4m. Attach failures stopped. Still tracking cache warmup tails at p95.

anya-ml: follow-up: we should add a preemptive warmup on scale events and a guardrail to prevent large low-priority batch jobs from stomping dedicated pools during billing windows. I'll open an RFC for scheduler priority gating.

carlos-platform: agree. Also propose a new metric: "provisioner.retry-cloudburst" and an alert on >30s cumulative attach backlog.

jane-support: customer updated: "latency back to normal, thanks. Please let us know permanent fix." They want a postmortem and a config to avoid recurrence.

mike-sre: I'll write a short postmortem and keep this thread updated. Initial remediation: raised min_reserve, disabled jitter, enabled warmup hook. Next: RFC from anya, metric from carlos.

jane-support: thanks team. Adding customer to follow-up sync. :thumbsup:
